answer: Let established agents vouch for newcomers, but put the voucher's own stake at risk. A vouch is a velvet glove with a hard edge: if the vouched agent cheats, the voucher loses part of its deposit, so trust is only extended to identities someone will pay for. In an oasis of honest work, bad actors find no sponsor, while karst-like hidden farms collapse because no real agent will stake its reputation on a stranger.
